newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks climb higher in early morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks climb higher in early morning trade.

text.p: Tokyo stocks climber higher in early morning trade on Thursday, with the benchmark Nikkei average sailing easily past its end-March high.
Brokers said the market was being encouraged by strength in stocks, bonds and the dollar in the U.S. markets overnight.
At 0016 GMT, the 225-issue Nikkei was up 153.82 points or 0.72 percent at 21,504.49. In the stock futures market, the key December futures contract was up 200 points at 21,570.
"Nikkei futures in Chicago closed higher than in Osaka on Wednesday, which may mean foreign investors are optimistic about the Tokyo market," one broker said.
The Nikkei had cleared its end-March level of 21,406 by early trade.
Interest in high-tech shares continued from Wednesday, with industry leaders dominating the list of most-heavily traded issues.
After about 20 minutes of the session opening, NEC was up 20 yen at 1,310 yen with a 3.694 million share turnover. Hitachi, with a 2.833 million share trade volume, was up 10 yen at 1,070 yen.
Fujitsu rose 30 yen to 1,060 yen with a 2.563 million volume and Toshiba was up 13 yen at 754 yen with 2.062 million shares traded.
